title: Hash map
short: Find anything by its name in one step.
what: A hash map stores pairs: a key and its value. You give it the key, and it jumps straight to the value without searching. In Python it is the dict.
analogy: A coat check. You hand over ticket 42 and the attendant walks straight to hook 42. Nobody checks every coat.

frames.label: ages
frames.say: Start with an empty dict called ages.

frames.label: ages
frames.say: ages["ann"] = 31 stores a pair: the key "ann" and the value 31.

frames.label: ages
frames.say: Add two more people. Each insert takes about the same tiny time, however big the dict gets.

frames.label: ages
frames.say: ages["bo"] jumps straight to bo's row. No loop over ann first.

frames.label: ages
frames.say: Writing to a key that exists replaces its value. Keys are unique, so ann still has one row.

frames.label: ages
frames.say: "dee" in ages checks for a key in one step too. Use it, or .get(), before reading a key that may be missing.

when: Count how many times each thing appears
Look something up by name or id
Find a partner that adds up to a target
Group items that share a key
python:
ages = {}
ages["ann"] = 31
ages["bo"] = 25
print(ages["bo"])
print("dee" in ages)
print(ages.get("dee", 0))

from collections import Counter
print(Counter("banana"))
cost: Find a value without its key
watch: Reading a missing key with ages[k] raises KeyError. Use .get(k, default) or check k in ages.
Keys must be unchangeable: strings, numbers, tuples. A list cannot be a key.
O(1) is the average. Order of keys is insertion order, not sorted.
